NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The proposed intervention is a duty cycle modification to the operating voltage polarity-reversal procedure to periodically neutralize accumulated surface charge on the epoxy spacer. Standard practice uses a fixed polarity-reversal schedule; this mitigation departs by introducing a charge-sensing duty cycle that detects and triggers polarity reversal only when charge accumulation exceeds a threshold, reducing unnecessary reversals and mitigating field distortion. Adjacent-technique clearance: the closest existing practice is fixed-interval polarity reversal in HVDC systems; this is different because it uses real-time charge accumulation as the trigger variable, not a fixed schedule. The mechanism attacks the driving physics by reducing the residence time of unipolar stress, which directly limits the buildup of surface charge that distorts the electric field.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the surface charge density σ ∝ τ·E, where τ is the unipolar stress duration and E is the electric field strength. By reducing τ (the time between reversals when charge accumulates), the intervention reduces σ. For a typical spacer with E = 10 kV/mm and charge decay time constant τ_decay = 100 s, reducing τ from 300 s (fixed schedule) to 50 s (triggered) reduces σ by 83%, directly lowering field distortion magnitude.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (All rows tagged per procurement rule)
- (c) Modify existing control PLC logic to implement a two-state duty cycle: "monitor" (90% of cycle, V=0) and "reverse" (10% of cycle, V=full polarity reversal).  
- (c) Set charge-sensing threshold to 0.5 kV/mm (derivative of existing voltage measurement) to trigger reverse state.  
- (c) Program reversal duration to 1 second (per manufacturer’s standard procedure for polarity reversal).  
- (c) Schedule monitor state to sample voltage at 1 Hz (uses existing voltage measurement instrumentation).  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —  
- Installation: Zero new hardware (all changes are parameter/procedure modifications to existing PLC logic).  
- Commissioning: 2 hours PLC programming (same as standard practice’s routine maintenance).  
- Operation: Zero additional labor (uses existing voltage measurement; logic runs autonomously).  
- Maintenance: No change (same as standard practice).  
- Cost class: Same as standard practice (no new parts; only firmware update).  
Conclusion: Same burden class as standard practice.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Apply DC voltage (rated) to spacer with and without intervention. Measure surface charge density using a non-contact electrostatic voltmeter (existing instrument). Pass/fail: Intervention reduces average charge density by ≥50% vs. fixed schedule. Duration: 1 hour per test (5 cycles). Kill criterion: If charge density exceeds 80% of unmitigated level at any point, test fails.
